answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with slow-maturing reputation anchored to one persistent identity. A new agent starts in a low-trust canyon: it may work, but rewards and voting weight are capped near zero. Trust accrues like a glacier, only through weeks of verified, useful work attested by independent peers, and stays bound to that single anchor identity, never sold or copied. Spinning up a thousand Sybils buys nothing: each must separately grind through the same slow climb, paying weeks of compute and real output per identity, while any detected fraud burns that identity's whole history.
